sentences.text: This appeal has been filed seeking for setting aside the judgment and award in L.A.C. No.249/1996 on the file of the Addl. Senior Civil Judge, Jamakhandi and the appellant seeks for enhancement by enhancing the market value at Rs.2,35,224/- with statutory benefits.

2. Brief facts relevant for the purpose of disposal are that the land of the claimant was notified for acquisition under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 for acquiring for the purpose of Housing Project on 22.01.1987.
The award was passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer determining the compensation initially at Rs.10,000/- per acre on 16.01.1990.

An application seeking reference was made and subsequently pursuant to such reference, the reference came to be partly allowed and compensation enhanced to Rs.2,17,800/- per acre as per the order of the reference court dated 26.10.2004.

The said order was taken up in appeal in M.F.A. No.3170/2005 by the Karnataka Housing Board and the NC: 2023:KHC-D:13126-DB said appeal came to be allowed in part while remanding the matter to the reference Court afresh.
Thereafter the reference Court by its order dated 07.08.2019, allowed the reference partially by enhancing the compensation at Rs.30,000/- per acre.
It is this order that has been assailed in the present proceedings.

3. Counsel for the appellant submits that though various grounds have been urged seeking enhancement, in light of the order passed in M.F.A. No.25157/2011 disposed of on 17.10.2019 with respect to land bearing R.S.No.624/2 and 624/3 situated at Jamakhandi relating to the same notification acquired for the same purpose, the market value has been fixed at Rs.2,35,224/- per acre in addition to solatium and statutory interest and other admissible statutory benefits the present appeal could be disposed off in terms of the said order.

It is submitted that judgment in the Miscellaneous First Appeal ought to be adopted as the land in the said appeal is adjacent to the subject matter of the present reference proceedings and relates to the acquisition under the same notification.

sentences.text:
Further it is submitted that the order of the reference Court in L.A.C.No.250/1996 which is a connected matter was heard along with present reference i.e., L.A.C.
No.249/1996 and both were disposed off by common order which was the subject matter of M.F.A.
No.3170/2005 and both the references were the subject matter of the same appeal and after setting aside the order of the reference Court under a common judgment, matter was remanded.
However,

subsequent to remand and only one of the reference case i.e., L.A.C. No.250/1996 was disposed off and which has come up in appeal in M.F.A. No.25157/2011, and disposed off on 17.10.2019, fixing the market value at Rs.2,35,224 per acre apart from other statutory benefits.
Accordingly it is submitted that other reference in L.A.C. No.249/1996 ought to be disposed of taking note of the market value fixed in M.F.A. No.251257/2011.

4. Insofar as learned counsel appearing for the beneficiary as well as the State do not controvert the said assertion relating to fixation of market value in M.F.A. NC: 2023:KHC-D:13126-DB No.25157/2011 and also are unable to controvert the assertion that the acquisition that was for the same purpose and lands in M.F.A. No.25157/2011 and L.A.C. No.249/1996 are adjacent and similarly situated.
5. Heard both sides.
6.

The question that falls for consideration is:
"Whether a case is made out for enhancement of compensation by taking note of the fixation of compensation for similarly situated lands under the same notification in M.F.A. No.25157/2011?"
7.

After hearing both the sides, it comes out clearly from the records on perusal of the judgment in M.F.A. No.25157/2011 that the lands in the aforesaid appeal i.e. bearing R.S. No.624/2 and 624/3 situated at Jamakhandi was the subject matter of 4(1) notification published on 22.01.1987 under which notification, the lands of the present appellant in Sy.No.627/3/2 measuring 5 acres 23 guntas has been notified.

The purpose of acquisition was for construction of houses under HUDCO NC:
2023:KHC-D:13126-DB scheme.
The lands belonging to the same village are adjacent, dry lands and having same potentiality.

8. There is no dispute insofar as order passed L.A.C. No.250/1996 (consequent upon the remand)
this court by a considered judgment in M.F.A. No.25157/2011, has fixed the compensation at Rs.2,35,224/- per acre.
The relevant paragraphs are extracted herein below:
"16. The appellant in order to prove the case have examined three witnesses namely P.W.1 to P.W.3 and have exhibited documents namely Exs.P-1 to P-22.
On the other hand, respondents have examined two witnesses namely R.W.1 and R.W.2 and got exhibited 13 documents namely Exs.R-1 to R- 13.

sentences.text: Admittedly, in view of the admission made by R.W.2 in his cross-examination, the lands in question are situated at a distance of 1 k.m. away from Jamkhandi Town.

From the cross-examination of R.W.2, it is evident that the lands in question are situate at Kunchanur - Bilagi road and it has further been admitted by him that the land bearing Sy. Nos.628 and 627 are adjacent to each other and land bearing Sy.
No.628 was converted for non- agricultural purposes in the year 1975 itself.

It has NC: 2023:KHC-D:13126-DB further been admitted by him that land bearing Sy.
No.630/1A, 630/1B, 635/1/1, 635/1/2, 635/2/B, 638/3, 639/3, 752/27, 4/2/2, 9/1 and Sy. Nos.109- 113 of Kumbar Halla Village and R.S. Nos.7 and 8 of Jamkhandi Village are already converted for non- agricultural purposes.
18. It is not in dispute that Jamkhandi Town is the headquarter of Revenue Sub Division which has industries, education institution and all commercial house.
From perusal of Ex.P-15, it is evident that the lands in question are surrounded by lands which have already been converted for non-agricultural purposes.
Therefore, in our considered opinion, the lands in question have potentiality for the non-agricultural use.

19. In view of the well settled legal propositions that the sale deeds in respect of small plots of land can furnish the basis for the determination of market value of large tracts of lands provided appropriate deductions are made specially when the agricultural lands are situate in close proximities towards city.
20.

In the instant case, as already stated supra, the agricultural lands in question are situate within a distance of 1 k.m. from the Jamkhandi Town which is headquarter of the Revenue Sub Division having industries, Education Institution and Sugar NC:
2023:KHC-D:13126-DB Factories.
It is also pertinent to mention here that the land is situated on a highway.

The appellant has produced the copy of the sale deeds Exs.P-7 to P-9 which have been executed in respect of the lands admeasuring 43,560 square feet in Jamkhandi Town and have been executed on 05.05.1986, 19.09.1986 and 14.10.1986 respectively.

Therefore, the aforesaid sale deeds which have been executed prior to issuance of notification under Section 4(1) of the Act which was issued on 22.01.1987, in our considered opinion can be taken to the basis for determining the market value of the lands in question provided appropriate deductions are made.

21. We are conscious of the fact that the sale deeds pertain to small pieces of lands which are situate in Jamkhandi town, whereas the lands in question are agricultural lands which are situate at a distance of 1 k.m. from Jamkhandi town and has a potentiality for non-agricultural use.
However, as stated supra, some element of guess work is always inherent in determination of the market value of the properties.

22. Therefore, if Exs.P-7 to P-9 are taken into account which are sale deeds executed in respect of small plots of land, the market value of the lands of the appellant comes to Rs.7,84,080/- per acre.

However, as stated supra, appropriate deductions are Smt.Akkubai Bhartar vs The Land Acquisition Officer on 7 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63253575/
4 required to be made.

sentences.text: In the fact situation of the case, NC: 2023:KHC-D:13126-DB we are inclined to deduct 70% on account of development charges.
Therefore, the market value of the land of the appellant is assessed at Rs.2,35,224/- per acre.

23. So far as finding recorded by the Reference Court that sale deeds Exs.P-7 to P-9 cannot be taken into consideration for determination of market value of the land is in contravention of the decisions of the Supreme Court which has been referred to in the preceding paragraph.
Therefore, we are not inclined to agree with the aforesaid finding.
24. The Reference Court has relied on Ex.R-8 for determination of market value of the land of the appellant at the rate of Rs.30,000/- per acre.

However, it is pertinent to mention here that Ex.R-R8, the market value of the lands situate in Jamkhandi Town has been determined with reference to the land which is situate in Bilagi town,
which is a different Taluk.
However, the aforesaid aspect of the matter has not been taken into account by the Reference Court.
Therefore, we set aside the finding of the Reference Court insofar as it pertains to placing reliance of Ex.R8 for determination of the market value of the land.

Similarly, in the state of evidence on record, the findings recorded by the Reference Court that the market value of the lands of the appellant is Rs.30,000/- per acre also cannot be up held for the reasons which we have assigned supra.
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:13126-DB Accordingly, it is held that the appellant shall be entitled to market value of the lands in question at the rate of Rs.2,35,224/- per acre, in addition to solatium and statutory interest which are admissible to the appellants under various heads as prescribed under the Act.
To the aforesaid extent, the award passed by the Reference Court is modified.
In the result, the appeal is partly allowed with costs."
9. It is clear that there cannot be any different stand taken in light of the lands being notified under the same notification and the purpose of acquisition is the same.
On principle of parity, both the landowners are required to be treated on the same lines.

Accordingly, the compensation determined in L.A.C. No.249/1996 at Rs.30,000/- per acre for dry land is enhanced to Rs.2,35,224/- per acre in addition to solatium, statutory interest and other statutory benefits under various heads of the Act.
Accordingly, the point for consideration is held - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:13126-DB in the affirmative and the appeal is disposed off with costs.
T.C.R. to be sent back.
